COMM-06 — PSV Objection Handling Guide ​

Sprint: PSV-COMM-001 Wave 3 Audience: Salesperson (internal reference — not shared with prospect) Purpose: Prepared responses to the 5 most common objections Usage: Review before every demo. Do not read aloud — internalize the logic.

Principle: Objection = Unmet Question ​

An objection is never a rejection. It is always one of three things:

1. Missing information  → they don't understand something yet
2. Unaddressed fear     → they have a concern they haven't voiced
3. Legitimate risk      → they have real business constraints

The goal is to identify which one — and respond to that, not to the surface objection.

Objection 1 — "Mere Paas Already ERP Hai" ​

What they really mean:

"I've already spent money on software. Why do I need more?"

The misunderstanding to correct: ERP tracks what the brand dispatched. PSV tracks what the distributor actually sold. These are two completely different datasets.

Response:

"Bilkul — ERP hona chahiye. ERP aapki primary sales track karta hai — kya dispatch hua, invoice kya bana, stock aapke warehouse mein kya hai.

PSV woh karta hai jo ERP nahi karta: distributor ne us stock mein se kitna becha? Kitna bacha hai? Kitne hafte ka cover hai?

ERP aapka picture complete karta hai aapke godown tak. PSV us picture ko distributor ke godown tak extend karta hai."

Proof point: "Show the slide: ERP stops at dispatch invoice. PSV starts there."

Follow-up question:

"Aapka ERP aapko batata hai ki Pune distributor ke paas Size 8 ka kitna stock hai abhi?" (They will say no. That's the opening.)

Objection 2 — "Data Share Kyun Karun?" ​

What they really mean (usually the distributor saying this):

"I don't want the brand to have leverage over me." OR: "This feels like surveillance."

The fear to address: This is a trust objection, not a technical one. Do not show features. Address the fear first.

Response:

"Yeh sawaal seedha hai — isliye main seedha answer deta hoon.

PSV mein brand ko sirf Sell-Through % aur stock levels dikhte hain. Aapki pricing, aapke customers, aapke margins — kuch nahi jaata.

Aur honestly — yeh data aapke liye bhi useful hai. Aapko pata chalega ki konsa item 90 din se nahi bika aur aapka capital lock hua pada hai.

Yeh mutual visibility hai — surveillance nahi. Brand ko wahi dikhta hai jo aap dikhana chahte ho."

If they push further:

"Pilot mein hum milke decide karte hain ki exactly kaunsa data brand ko jaata hai. Koi mandatory full disclosure nahi hai."

Do NOT say: "We will never share your data with anyone." (Over-promising on privacy.)

Objection 3 — "Yeh Sirf Brand Ke Liye Useful Hai" ​

What they really mean:

"What's in it for me? I'm the one doing extra work."

The unaddressed value: PSV surfaces information the distributor doesn't have either — dead stock, slow movers, transfer opportunities. Most distributors discover dead stock only during annual physical audits.

Response:

"Main samajhta hoon yeh concern — kyunki normally brand wali tools sirf brand ko data deti hain, distributor ko kuch nahi milta.

PSV mein aapko teen cheezein milti hain:

Pehla — aapka dead stock automatically identify hota hai. Aapko annual audit ka wait nahi karna.

Doosra — jab brand ke saath baat karte ho reorder ke liye, aapke paas numbers hote hain, arguments nahi.

Teesra — aapko pata rehta hai konsa size kab khatam honewala hai — aap proactively reorder karte ho, rush order nahi."

Proof point: Use COMM-03 Scenario 2 (Meera, Nagpur — ₹4.1L dead stock recovered).

Objection 4 — "Team Use Nahi Karegi" ​

What they really mean:

"This is a change management problem I don't want to deal with." OR: "The effort to train people is higher than the benefit."

The real concern: Adoption, not capability.

Response:

"Yeh valid concern hai — har tool ka yahi hota hai.

Isliye humne PSV ko Excel-first design kiya hai. Team ko kuch naya sikhne ki zaroorat nahi — jo already Excel use karta hai, woh PSV use kar sakta hai.

Pehle hafte hum saath karte hain — onboarding session 30 minute ka hai. Template hum dete hain. Format hum handle karte hain.

Aur pilot ke 30 din mein — agar team weekly upload kar rahi hai, engagement metric track hota hai. Agar log use nahi kar rahe — hum week 2 mein hi pata kar lete hain aur adjust karte hain."

Follow-up:

"Aapke operations mein kaun distributor se directly baat karta hai? Woh ek banda hi kaafi hai pilot ke liye."

Objection 5 — "Pilot Ke Baad Kya Hoga?" ​

What they really mean:

"Am I signing up for something I can't exit?" OR: "Will you pressure me into a contract after 30 days?"

The fear to address: Lock-in, hidden commitment, pricing ambush.

Response:

"Seedha bata deta hoon — pilot ke baad teen raaste hain.

Pehla — agar data dikhata hai ki PSV ne value diya: hum rollout conversation karte hain — aur more distributors mein extend karte hain.

Doosra — agar kuch specific gap tha — WOC tracking useful tha lekin dead stock detection relevant nahi tha — hum specifically wahi fix karte hain aur re-pilot option dete hain.

Teesra — agar value nahi mili: aap exit karo. Koi contract nahi. Pilot ke baad koi automatic billing nahi.

Pricing conversation pilot review ke baad hogi — data ke saath. Bina data ke pricing discuss karna dono ke liye waste hai."

If they ask for pricing upfront anyway:

"Pricing structure hai — pilot ke baad share karta hoon jab numbers samne hain. Tabhi conversation meaningful hogi."

Objection Quick-Reference Card ​

ObjectionCategoryKey Response Move
"Already ERP hai"Missing infoShow ERP vs PSV scope gap
"Data share kyun?"Fear (surveillance)Address trust first, features second
"Sirf brand ke liye"Unaddressed valueShow 3 distributor benefits
"Team use nahi karegi"Adoption riskExcel-first design + onboarding support
"Pilot ke baad kya?"Lock-in fearThree clear exit paths

Objection Severity Guide ​

Objection about data privacy    → HIGH severity. Stop demo. Address directly. Resume only after resolved.
Objection about ERP             → MEDIUM. Quick 2-minute correction. Continue demo.
Objection about team adoption   → MEDIUM. Address, then offer Week 1 onboarding support.
Objection about post-pilot      → LOW. Address, then reframe toward pilot start.
Objection about pricing         → DEFER. "After pilot — data se baat karte hain."

What NOT To Do ​

DO NOT:     Argue with the objection
DO NOT:     Dismiss it as uninformed
DO NOT:     Promise things that aren't in the product
DO NOT:     Answer pricing without COMM-04 structure
DO NOT:     Continue demo over an unresolved trust objection

Governance: Jawahar R. Mallah, Founder & Chief Architect, AITDLInternal tool — responses are starting points, not scripts. Adapt to the conversation.
